payload.title: The cqrs adapter reads only controllers/** and *.controller.ts, so the 26 production GraphQL resolver files that match its own rule-2 pattern (@InjectRepository or Repository<T> injected into the request layer) are never read and never reported
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/cqrs-adapter.tool.json:22 (allowed_read_globs repeat the same two globs, so the kernel snapshot never hands over a resolver)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md layer rule 1 (no layer skipping between the request layer and the repository); the adapter's rule 2 states the same defect for controllers and the resolver is the request layer of the GraphQL services.
payload.notes: Counted at the revision: 113 production *.resolver.ts files against 92 controllers in the adapter's scope, and 26 of those resolvers match the adapter's rule-2 pattern (auth, farm, hr, hydroponics, notification and sensor services). The same code in a *.controller.ts would raise controller_injects_repository_directly (HIGH cap); in a resolver it is silently not raised, so the adapter under-reports the layering defect on the majority of the request surface. CLAUDE.md and the nested service CLAUDE.md files do not exempt resolvers, and the registry already files a resolver reading repositories directly as a layering violation (SENSOR-MEDIUM-073, FARM-HIGH-088), so the exclusion is a detector gap and not a recorded decision. Close condition: Add `apps/**/*.resolver.ts` to cqrs_adapter SCANNED_GLOBS and to the manifest declared_scope and allowed_read_globs (test_adapter_scope_narrow pins the two together) and add a fixture with a resolver that injects a repository; if the operator decides resolvers are exempt, write that into manifest premise 1 and CLAUDE.md layer rule 1 so the exclusion is a stated rule. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
